notes.summary: Reconstructed ordinary middle-positive Borel multiplication and all-stage positivity: locally bounded generated-Psh u gives positive doubly closed D(uT), over every original field and analytic scope. This is separate-product positivity, not P21.3 independence.
notes.detailedSummary: The supplied unreviewed bounded-generated argument is reconstructed using compact middle-positive test decomposition, signed coefficient Radon measures, and positive-definite exterior-power domination on each finite moment presentation. It supplies an actual order-zero current for locally bounded Borel coefficients. In every sheafified successor stage, a locally bounded final section bounds decreasing predecessors below; finite upper-semicontinuous first predecessors bound them above on each compact. Fixed coefficient measures then give bounded decreasing convergence. Limit stages are handled by ordinary locality, and a set-cardinality stabilization argument exhausts generated Psh. No reverse continuous-Psh recognition, continuous predecessors, reducedness, smoothness, nontrivial valuation, or strongly-positive spanning is assumed. Ordered products and the two-sign sufficient multiplier condition follow. The general continuous equal-curvature difference has not been shown to satisfy that two-sign condition.
notes.text:
Research proof, unverified. Let K be any complete non-Archimedean field, possibly trivially valued, and X good, separated, strict, boundaryless, pure of dimension n>=2. On every ordinary open W, let T be an ordinary middle-positive current of bidegree (p,p), 0<=p<=n-1, with d'T=d''T=0. Write D=d'd''. Retain the canonical integration current and actual generic component lengths. The theorem proved here is: every locally bounded real section u of generated CLD Psh has an ordinary Borel product uT, and D(uT) is middle-positive and doubly closed. It is not a claim that equal canonical curvatures give equal products against arbitrary T.

Exact external calculus inputs are CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2 (25 July 2025): ordinary opens and compact neighbourhoods (11.1.7), calibrated analytic-domain compatibility (15.7.1–2), good Hausdorff implies locally holomorphically/differentially separated and compact smooth cutoffs/localization/density (15.2.2–9); compact symmetric tests decompose as differences of compact middle-positive tests on this almost-good scope (6.5.2); positive scalar currents have unique Radon measures (7.2.8), and positive complementary tests give coefficient measures (7.2.11); the signed matrix cone is positive semidefinite on exterior powers and face positivity is checked on tangent faces (1.2.6–7, 1.10.1); chart topology is cellwise with fixed supports and moments (7.1.1–3), compact moment images are polyhedral (only that part of 12.2.4); currents form ordinary sheaves (7.1.6–7), differentials are weakly continuous and satisfy their square-zero, anticommutation and duality identities (7.7.1–5), and smooth s gives D(sT)=Ds wedge T (8.5.3–4). Positive smooth factors preserve middle positivity (7.2.7(b)). These scope hypotheses hold on every original ordinary open in either valuation regime. The disputed printed moment dimension equality and reverse Psh/CPsh recognition are not used.

For a symmetric compact complementary test beta=eta1-eta2 with eta_i middle-positive, define mu_beta=mu_eta1-mu_eta2. The result is independent of the decomposition: competing signed measures agree on smooth compact scalars, hence on continuous compact scalars by density, hence are equal. It is linear, and its intrinsic support lies in supp beta by applying that density within the complement. Define <bT,beta>=integral b dmu_beta for locally bounded Borel b, and discard antisymmetric tests. To verify ordinary order-zero continuity rather than just linearity, localize to rho f* a in one moment chart, rho>=0 compact smooth. Take a compact analytic neighbourhood C of supp rho inside that chart, formed from finitely many affinoids when necessary. The moment image P has finitely many tangent faces. Fix Euclidean Theta=sum dx_i' wedge dx_i''. Theta^q is positive definite on each qth exterior tangent space for q=n-p, and both restrictions vanish when the face dimension is below q. A uniform constant c for the finite presentation gives c||a||_(P,0)Theta^q +/- a>=0 for every symmetric a. For q=0 this is the scalar bound. Coefficient measures imply |mu_(rho f*a)|<=c||a||_(P,0)mu_(rho f*Theta^q). Therefore |<bT,rho f*a>|<=c||b||_(supp rho)||a||_(P,0)<T,rho f*Theta^q>. Localized chart topology proves order-zero continuity; no strongly-positive spanning is used. Equality of coefficient measures under compact extension by zero proves restriction compatibility.

For a decreasing bounded sequence b_j to b and any fixed positive coefficient measure on compact C, g_j=b_j-b decreases to zero and is bounded by M. The Borel sets E_j={g_j>=epsilon} decrease to the empty set, so their finite measures tend to zero. The estimate integral g_j<=epsilon mu(C)+M mu(E_j) proves convergence by letting j tend to infinity and then epsilon to zero. Applied to each positive test measure, it proves b_jT->bT weakly. Locally uniform nets also converge after multiplication by fixed T, by the bound ||b_a-b||_C<T,eta1+eta2>. No bounded-pointwise-convergence assertion for arbitrary nets is made.

Reconstruct generated Psh from Definition 8.1.1 and Lemma 8.1.4. Rank zero is smooth positive-Hessian functions; successors are ordinary-local decreasing sequential limits of preceding ranks; limit ranks are ordinary-local earlier-rank membership. These are increasing sheaves. Upper semicontinuity is preserved since {inf_j u_j<a}=union_j{u_j<a}, and is local at limit ranks; finite sections are Borel. All open/section pairs form a set, so the increasing chain has an equal-successor stage by a cardinal argument. That stage is fixed, sheafified, contains the generators, and is decreasing-sequentially closed, hence equals the minimal Psh sheaf. No extraneous local-integrability condition is inserted.

Induct simultaneously on every ordinary open and rank for locally bounded real final sections. Rank zero gives D(uT)=Du wedge T>=0. At a successor choose a neighbourhood on which u_j decreases to u. Every u_j is finite because u_j>=u and +infinity is never permitted. The final u bounds each u_j locally below; upper semicontinuity bounds each finite u_j locally above. On each compact C there are a,b with a<=u<=u_j<=u1<=b, independently of j. Every predecessor is therefore locally bounded and qualifies for induction even if discontinuous. Fixed-measure convergence gives D(u_jT)->D(uT); positivity and symmetry pass to the limit. At a limit ordinal, use earlier membership on each ordinary neighbourhood and current locality. Stabilization proves the theorem, and differential square-zero identities give both closedness equations. Scalar tests when p=n-1 and degree (n-1,n-1) tests when p=0 are included. No generic multiplicities have been discarded.

Consequently ordered differentiation by m locally bounded generated potentials is positive and doubly closed when m<=n-p. If h and -h themselves are generated Psh and locally bounded, then D(hT) and its negative are positive; compact positive-test decomposition and symmetry force zero. An arbitrary h=U-V with D[h]=0 has not been put in this two-sign class.

The full proof and primary premises are in P21.3-core.md, P21.3-argument.md, and P21.3-paper.tex/PDF. Literal evidence, versioned LF intervals and hashes are in P21.3-primary-evidence.md, premises.json, and source-manifest.json. The bound CLD text hash is 64846cb00926267c6238d1afac61b5eaed0a0e3a6349725738f9b1bf163de085; the complete text was not read in full. Rerun bash reproduce.sh. Finite integrity/schema checks and compilation are not mathematical acceptance. Original input and exact task/assignment extractions are frozen. No independent reviewer, other worker, install, network acquisition, or heavy computation was used.

notes.summary: Mixed symmetry is reconstructed for arbitrary original T with one continuous generated-Psh factor and one locally bounded generated-Psh factor. It also gives permutation independence with at most one discontinuous factor; it does not resolve signed curvature relations.
notes.detailedSummary: For p<=n-2, v continuous generated Psh and u locally bounded real generated Psh, D(uD(vT))=D(vD(uT)). Induction is over all sheafified ranks of u. The left limit uses fixed positive D(vT) coefficient measures; the right limit uses positive D(u_jT) and the fixed continuous multiplier v. The ordinary weak-multiplication argument extends to nets with eventual mass bounds, but is never used for a discontinuous varying-current multiplier. Adjacent swaps give all ordered products with at most one discontinuous factor. Subtracting two continuous factors yields a signed identity, whose right side still contains D(hT); zero canonical D[h] does not set this term to zero.
notes.text:
Research proof using n1's actual Borel products and all-stage positivity. Retain all original K,X,W,T hypotheses and canonical multiplicities. Assume 0<=p<=n-2, u locally bounded real generated Psh, and v finite continuous generated Psh. Both D(uT) and D(vT) are positive doubly closed by n1, so the products in D(uD(vT))=D(vD(uT)) are ordinary currents, including for discontinuous u.

First reconstruct weak multiplication. For positive S_a->S weakly, S is positive and symmetric by evaluation. For a compact symmetric test beta=eta1-eta2, the masses <S_a,eta1+eta2> converge, hence are eventually bounded even for a directed net. On their compact union approximate a fixed continuous v uniformly by a smooth g, using a compact cutoff and the smooth scalar density stated in n1. The pairing error is at most epsilon<S_a,eta1+eta2>+|<S_a-S,g beta>|+epsilon<S,eta1+eta2>. Take the current limit for fixed g, then epsilon to zero. Thus vS_a->vS. Locally uniform varying continuous v_a also works by the additional estimate ||v_a-v||_C<S_a,eta1+eta2>. This reconstructs CLD v2 Lemma 8.5.1 and its fixed-function net version; no whole-net mass bound or discontinuous multiplier is assumed.

For a smooth even-degree doubly closed form gamma, differentiation commutes with wedge gamma by the ordinary Leibniz rule in duality. Also b(T wedge gamma)=(bT) wedge gamma whenever T and T wedge gamma are positive and b is locally bounded Borel: their coefficient measures agree on smooth scalars and hence agree identically. The same construction is independent of decompositions into finite differences of positive currents, since equality of current functionals determines their signed coefficient measures. These are consequences of the exact ordinary inputs in n1, not strong-current product assertions.

Fix v and T, and induct over u's sheafified ordinal rank on every ordinary subopen. For smooth u, Du is positive smooth and doubly closed; therefore D(uD(vT))=Du wedge D(vT)=D((vT) wedge Du)=D(v(T wedge Du))=D(vD(uT)). At a successor, the locally bounded final u gives finite locally bounded predecessors u_j decreasing to u, with one compact bound as proved in n1. The inductive equality holds for every u_j. Fixed-measure bounded convergence for the positive fixed D(vT) gives u_jD(vT)->uD(vT). Separately, fixed-T convergence gives D(u_jT)->D(uT), and every current here is positive. Since v is continuous, the weak-multiplication estimate gives vD(u_jT)->vD(uT). Weak continuity of D proves the desired identity. At limit ranks use earlier membership locally; current locality and stabilization finish all stages. No CPsh recognition or continuity of u_j is used.

For m factors with m<=n-p and at most one discontinuous locally bounded generated factor, each adjacent interchange has a continuous factor, so this theorem applies to its inner positive closed current. Outer operations on equal positive currents preserve equality. Thus the ordered recursion is permutation-independent in this scope. This is not an interchange theorem for two arbitrary discontinuous factors.

For h=U-V with U,V continuous generated Psh and continuous generated v, subtraction gives D(hD(vT))=D(vD(hT)); the right side means the difference of products with the positive currents D(UT) and D(VT). Equal canonical D[U],D[V] identifies D(h delta_X)=0, not D(hT). The signed symmetry retains D(hT) and cannot prove it vanishes without an additional argument.

The complete proofs are Theorem 2 and Corollaries 2.1–2.2 in P21.3-core.md and P21.3-paper.tex/PDF, with full primary weak-multiplication evidence at LF10257–10281 of CLD v2. The exact bound raw file is sources/cld-weak-multiplier-bound.txt, hash 0448ea1b480496814c9d81b4a5443f7d6efbb05b91582305b117704008184860. The normalized slice sources/cld-weak-multiplier.txt adds one trailing newline and has hash 0eec1c45dfec34af7fb8e231160cc24fd3ef9b8f6dc1185fb8eedd1905483114. notes.summary: New closure beyond the supplied continuous-factor proposal: D(vS) preserves continuous-pair compatibility for every locally bounded generated-Psh v, even discontinuous. Smooth positive closed decorations and weak positive limits also preserve it; arbitrary-current exhaustion remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Orient the one-continuous-factor theorem with the differentiating bounded v as the potentially discontinuous factor and the original U,V as continuous factors. If S is pair-compatible, D(US)=D(VS) are equal positive currents, so their actual Borel products with v are equal; symmetry then proves D(UD(vS))=D(VD(vS)). This works on each arbitrary subopen, for p<=n-2, and retains all original fields, middle positivity, singularities and nilpotents. Iterated differentiation by several discontinuous potentials preserves the continuous-pair property without claiming their permutation symmetry. Starting at delta_X yields a constructed compatible-current class, but no local weak density theorem for arbitrary T is supplied. The exact missing analytic exhaustion and the unchanged original target are stated in the paper and status.json.
notes.text:
Research proof depending on n1 and n2. A positive doubly closed S on W is pair-compatible if on every ordinary O subset W, all finite continuous generated-Psh U,V with D[U]=D[V] satisfy D(US)=D(VS). This is the original continuous-pair condition for that current, not a classification. The original canonical delta_X is pair-compatible because U delta_X=[U]. It is middle-positive by canonical calibrated integration and doubly closed by boundaryless Stokes (CLD v2 15.7.1, 5.8.1–5 and 7.7.4); these hypotheses apply to the original pure boundaryless X and its ordinary opens. Its actual generic lengths are retained.

The new result is closure under D(vS) for any locally bounded real generated-Psh v, possibly discontinuous, when S has degree p<=n-2. Positivity and closedness of D(vS), D(US), D(VS) follow from n1. On an arbitrary O carrying an admissible pair, apply n2 with the potentially discontinuous factor u=v|O and the continuous factor U, and separately V. It gives D(UD(vS))=D(vD(US)) and D(VD(vS))=D(vD(VS)). Pair compatibility of S identifies the positive currents D(US)=D(VS). Their Borel products with the same v are equal by n1's intrinsic coefficient measure construction. The desired equality follows. Since O was arbitrary, this is an every-open assertion for D(vS). No discontinuous multiplier has been passed through weak convergence on varying currents. This extends the continuous differentiating potential proposed in supplied unreviewed new103.

Compatible currents are also closed under addition and nonnegative scaling in a fixed degree. Ordinary locality follows by restricting the pair and using the current sheaf. A positive weak net S_a->S preserves compatibility: on each subopen, the original continuous U,V multiply that net weakly by n2, and D passes to the limit. Both closedness equations and positivity pass on fixed tests. For a smooth middle-positive doubly closed form gamma, the wedge is positive closed, and n2's smooth-factor identities give D(h(S wedge gamma))=D(hS) wedge gamma=0 for h=U-V. Require p+degree(gamma)<=n-1. These proofs impose no global paracompactness or field restriction.

Starting with delta_X, these operations define actual compatible positive currents, including ordered iterated differentiation by several locally bounded discontinuous generated potentials. The statement does not interchange two discontinuous factors and does not quantify over discontinuous pairs. The compatible current has degree at most n-1; a top-degree ordered product may exist but no further required pair step is counted.

The unproved analytic exhaustion is explicit: for every original K,X,p,W,T and x in W, find one ordinary neighbourhood N and a weakly convergent net of actual positive doubly closed degree-p currents on N, locally obtained from canonical delta_X by these operations, converging to T|N against every compact ordinary smooth test and every analytic-unit moment refinement. If proved, the weak closure just established would settle the original assertion locally and hence on every W. No such exhaustion is inferred from scalar smooth density, coefficient measure estimates, positive products, or the definition of compatibility. An alternative direct preservation theorem, a valid two-sign generating construction for an arbitrary equal-curvature difference on a fixed neighbourhood, or an actual admissible analytic counterexample is still needed.

This constructed-current closure is genuine partial progress, not a full solution or a restatement of a formal annihilator criterion. It does not silently restrict the ambient canonical Hessian equation to analytic curves or ascend it under transcendental scalar extension. No current lift to strong currents or product compatibility is assumed. The granted strict real-PL and pure-curve cases are not counted as universal coverage.

Theorem 3, the exact unproved analytic statement, and comparison with the residual catalogue appear in P21.3-core.md, P21.3-argument.md, and P21.3-paper.tex/PDF. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps, with status partial. Originals, primary evidence/hashes, rerun scripts, environment and build logs are preserved locally. Rerun bash reproduce.sh. Original P21.3 remains unresolved and candidate=false.

notes.summary: A fixed compact probability convolution kernel commuting with both split-torus monomial shears must be delta_0. This diagnoses one rigid regularization attempt, not all compatible regularizations or P21.3; no admissible analytic counterexample was obtained.
notes.detailedSummary: On the actual strict boundaryless analytic surface (G_m,Q2^2)^an, two Laurent monomial automorphisms induce the shears A(x,y)=(x+y,y) and B(x,y)=(x,x+y). A single translation convolution kernel commuting with both pullbacks is invariant under both shears. Compact support and iterates force every support point to have both coordinates zero, so a probability kernel is delta_0. Coordinate-dependent transformed kernels and directed finite-presentation regularization are not excluded. Ordinary partition-of-unity gluing separately preserves positivity but can lose both closedness equations. These are failed-route diagnostics, with no pair/current/test satisfying the original negative criterion. Compilation and finite checks establish reproducibility only; the full atom remains open.
notes.text:
Independent elementary diagnostic, not a solution of P21.3. Fix the actual analytic surface X=(G_m over Q_2)^2 analytified. It is good, separated, strict, smooth, boundaryless and pure of dimension two. The Laurent monomial maps (z1,z2)->(z1z2,z2) and (z1,z2)->(z1,z1z2) have monomial inverses, hence are analytic automorphisms. In logarithmic coordinates they induce A(x,y)=(x+y,y) and B(x,y)=(x,x+y), directly by multiplicativity of the norm. CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 12.1.1–4 supplies this analytic-torus and character/tropicalization setup; only these explicit maps are used.

Let mu be a compactly supported positive probability measure on R^2 and K_mu f(x)=integral f(x-z) dmu(z). If the same convolution operator commutes with pullback by A, evaluation at zero for every compact smooth f implies integral f(-Az) dmu(z)=integral f(-z) dmu(z). Uniqueness of finite Radon measures from smooth scalar tests gives A_*mu=mu; similarly B_*mu=mu. Thus the compact support is invariant under both invertible shears. If (x,y) lies in that support, all A^k(x,y)=(x+ky,y) lie there. Compactness forces y=0. Then all B^k(x,0)=(x,kx) lie there, forcing x=0. The support is {0} and mu=delta_0. Hence a nontrivial compact smooth probability mollifier cannot have these two fixed-kernel naturality properties.

This disproves only this rigid choice of one unchanged scalar kernel. Kernels can transform with coordinates, depend on the finite moment collection, or form a directed system. The result rules out none of those approaches and proves no failure of an all-refinement compatible analytic current regularization. It supplies no U,V,T or product defect. The torus itself is in established positive geometric ranges.

A separate direct Leibniz calculation explains why merely patching positive closed chart currents by nonnegative smooth partitions is insufficient: d'(sum rho_i R_i)=sum d'rho_i wedge R_i when each R_i is closed. The sum of rho_i being one does not cancel the right side unless further compatibility is present. In Euclidean dimension two, R1=[1], R2=2[1], rho1=rho, rho2=1-rho with nonconstant 0<rho<1 produce the positive but non-first-closed current [2-rho]. This is a failure of that gluing operation, not an original analytic counterexample. The ordinary differential Leibniz rule used here is CLD v2 3.3.10–12 and 7.7.1–5; both differential equations would need to be preserved by a successful regularizer.

These diagnostics accompany the genuinely proved calculus steps in the paper but do not fill the arbitrary-current exhaustion gap. The exact original every-field, every-open, every-current continuous-pair assertion remains unproved in this work. No analytic counterexample with separately admissible continuous generated-Psh potentials, upstairs canonical Hessian equality, a positive doubly closed current and a nonzero compact smooth test was constructed.

Proposition 4 and the gluing calculation are in P21.3-core.md and P21.3-paper.tex/PDF. Evidence is retained in P21.3-primary-evidence.md and the version/hash manifests.
